The '''2015–16 [[La Liga]]''' season (known as the ''Liga [[Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria|BBVA]]'' for sponsorship reasons) was the 85th since its establishment. [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] were the defending champions. The season began on 21 August 2015, and concluded on 15 May 2016.

Barcelona successfully retained the title (their 24th Liga overall) following a 3–0 win against [[Granada CF|Granada]] on the final matchday.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/la-liga-bbva/20160514/401793583944/campeones-a-lo-grande.html|title = El FC Barcelona, campeón a lo grande &#124; Liga BBVA|date = 15 May 2016}}</ref> Barcelona, [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and [[Atlético Madrid]] were engaged in an intense title race, with the three teams finishing with 91, 90 and 88 points respectively.

Barcelona's [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] finished as the league's top scorer, becoming the first player apart from [[Lionel Messi]] or [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] to do so since the [[2008–09 La Liga|2008–09 season]].

==Teams==
===Promotion and relegation (pre-season)===
A total of twenty teams contested the league, including seventeen sides from the [[2014–15 La Liga|2014–15 season]] and three promoted from the [[2014–15 Segunda División]]. This included the two top teams from the Segunda División, [[Real Betis]] and [[Sporting de Gijón|Sporting Gijón]], and the winners of the [[2015 Segunda División play-offs|play-offs]], [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Segunda División:Season Rules|url=http://www.scoresway.com/?sport=soccer&page=competition&id=12&view=rules|website=scoresway.com|access-date=22 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924123202/http://www.scoresway.com/?sport=soccer&page=competition&id=12&view=rules|archive-date=24 September 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

[[UD Almería|Almería]] and [[Córdoba CF|Córdoba]] were relegated to [[2015–16 Segunda División]] in the previous season, after spending two and one years in La Liga, respectively. [[Elche CF|Elche]] was administratively relegated despite finishing in 13th.<ref name="Elche">{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/en/news/official-statement-27|title=Official statement|publisher=LFP.es|date=5 June 2015}}</ref> Following the competition rules, [[SD Eibar|Eibar]], who finished 18th, remained in the league.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/en/news/javier-tebas-we-are-certain-the-royal-decree-will-soon-be-signed|title=Javier Tebas: "We are certain the Royal Decree will soon be signed"|publisher=LFP.es|date=25 March 2015}}</ref>

[[Real Betis]] was the first team from the [[2014–15 Segunda División|Segunda División]] to achieve promotion, after a one-year absence from La Liga, on 24 May 2015 after winning 3–0 over [[AD Alcorcón|Alcorcón]].<ref>{{cite web |title=A Primera por la puerta grande|url=http://www.marca.com/2015/05/24/futbol/2adivision/1432499778.html|newspaper=Marca |access-date=24 March 2015}}</ref>

On 7 June 2015, [[Sporting de Gijón|Sporting Gijón]] secured promotion on the final matchday, after their 3–0 win against Betis allowed the club to leapfrog [[Girona FC|Girona]], who drew their final match and could not retain second place and automatic promotion. Sporting returned to the top level after three years.

[[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] achieved promotion on 21 June 2015, after defeating [[Real Zaragoza|Zaragoza]] in the promotion play-off final on away goals. Las Palmas won the second 2–0 leg at home after losing the first leg away 3–1, and returned to the first division after thirteen years away. They also became the first island team to play in La Liga since [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]]'s relegation from the top flight in the [[2012–13 La Liga|2012–13 season]]. During those thirteen seasons, the club spent two of them in the third-tier [[Segunda División B]].

==Overview==
On 14 May 2016, [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] won their second consecutive and 24th overall La Liga title, following a 3–0 win over [[Granada CF|Granada]] at the [[Estadio Nuevo Los Cármenes]] on the final matchday.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-us/news/88/spain/2016/05/14/23516642/barcelona-wins-la-liga-title|title=Barcelona wins La Liga title|website=Goal.com|date=14 May 2016|access-date=30 May 2016}}</ref> [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] finished one point behind Barcelona as runners-up, having gone on a twelve-match win streak to close out the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36250293|publisher=BBC Sport|title=Deportivo La Coruna 0–2 Real Madrid|date=14 May 2016|access-date=30 May 2016}}</ref> [[Atlético Madrid]] ended the season three points off the top in third place, having been eliminated from title contention after a loss to [[Levante UD|Levante]] on the penultimate matchday.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36187568|publisher=BBC Sport|title=Levante 2–1 Atlético Madrid|date=8 May 2016|access-date=30 May 2016}}</ref>

Levante were the first team to be mathematically relegated to the [[2016–17 Segunda División|Segunda División]], following a 1–3 loss against [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] on 2 May 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurosport.com/football/levante-relegated-after-3-1-defeat-at-malaga_sto5558232/story.shtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161011060755/http://www.eurosport.com/football/levante-relegated-after-3-1-defeat-at-malaga_sto5558232/story.shtml|url-status=dead|archive-date=11 October 2016|title=Levante relegated after 3-1 defeat at Malaga|publisher=Eurosport|date=2 May 2016|access-date=30 May 2016}}</ref> On 15 May 2016, [[Sporting de Gijón|Sporting Gijón]] ensured they would remain in the top flight after defeating [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] 2–0 and taking advantage of [[Getafe CF|Getafe]]'s loss against [[Real Betis]], which saw Getafe relegated from La Liga for the first time in club history. [[Rayo Vallecano]] also went down despite winning their final match of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://en.as.com/en/2016/05/15/football/1463343024_658570.html|title=Sporting Gijón escape drop as Getafe, Rayo Vallecano go down|publisher=AS|date=15 May 2016|access-date=30 May 2016|archive-date=11 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180211071635/https://en.as.com/en/2016/05/15/football/1463343024_658570.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Zamora Trophy===
The [[Ricardo Zamora Trophy]] was awarded by newspaper ''[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]'' to the goalkeeper with the lowest ratio of goals conceded to matches played. A goalkeeper had to play at least 28 matches of 60 or more minutes to be eligible for the trophy.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/deporte/futbol/trofeos/2015-2016/zamora/primera.html|title=Trofeo Zamora La Liga Santander|newspaper=Marca|language=es}}</ref>

==Broadcasting rights==
[[Telefónica]] purchased the exclusive television broadcasting rights to telecast the 2015–16 season in Spain. [[Sky Sports]] had exclusive rights in the United Kingdom, and [[beIN Sports]] had exclusive rights to air the season in various countries, including the United States, Canada, [[MENA]], France and the Middle East.<ref>{{cite web| title=Spanish La Liga 2015-16 TV Channels Broadcast, Coverage| url=http://www.sportsmirchi.com/spanish-la-liga-2015-16-tv-channels-broadcast-coverage/|publisher= Sports Mirchi| access-date= 13 July 2015}}</ref> KBSN Sports had the exclusive television broadcasting rights in South Korea, apart from internet broadcasting.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kbsn.co.kr/sports/program_self_intro.do?pageIndex=1&searchBrdcstSn=0000000184&searchBdcstCode=sports&searchOnslfMnfctAt=N&searchMenuSn=110&searchMenuKnd=0001&searchCondition=0&searchKeyword=|publisher=KBSN|language=ko|title=프로그램 소개}}</ref>
